stem: A ketamine prescription is presented to a Massachusetts community pharmacy. Select all supported conclusions.

choices.text: Schedule III refill limits apply if refills are authorized.
Ketamine is Schedule II and can never be refilled.
Massachusetts treats ketamine as Schedule VI.
A five-day contiguous-state narcotic rule automatically governs every ketamine prescription.

explanation.core_reasoning: Apply each proposition independently. A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner. Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard. ketamine (Ketalar) is used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia. It is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.

choice_analysis.B: This statement imports Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.C: The proposition 'Covered outpatient dispensing is MassPAT-reportable.' is supported by Massachusetts pharmacy MassPAT dispensing-data reporting: Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
choice_analysis.D: This statement imports Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.E: This statement imports Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
